column1: # A screen of six by five pixels, the tables the kernels read, the jobs that
# draw on it and the screen they must leave. Every number here was worked out
# by hand from the definitions under src/; no other implementation is run to
#   tile    the eight entries row_fill samples
#   lut     the lookup table, 16 entries a row: row 0 leaves a value as it
#           is, row 1 turns v into 15 - v
#   offs    the row distances col_smear reads at
#   job     kernel and seven fields (- where a kernel has fewer):
#             col    x  y0  y1  start  step  period  row
#             row    y  x0  x1  u      du    row     -
#             smear  x  y0  y1  phase  period  row   -
#   screen  one row of the screen the jobs must leave, top row first
#   check   id, a job, then: short  status  moved
# The screen starts at 0 everywhere. A check runs on a fresh screen. `short`
# names a table declared one cell shorter than it is, or -. `status` is 0 OK,
# 2 ARITHMETIC, 3 BOUNDS. `moved` is, for a refusal, the number of pixels the
# call drew before it stopped, which a direct caller can still read.
# Column 1 takes the pattern in order: 1, 2, 3, 1, 2.
# Column 4, rows 1 to 3, steps by two from the last entry (3, 2, 1) through row 1 of the table: 12, 13, 14.
# Row 2 samples the tile every 1.5 entries: entries 0, 1, 3, 4, 6, 7, so 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 11. It crosses both columns.
# Column 1, rows 1 to 3, from its neighbours through row 1 of the table: row 1 reads row 0 (1 -> 14), row 2 reads row 3
# (1 -> 14), row 3 reads row 2, which this job has just drawn (14 -> 1).
# Checks. Each edge has the case just inside it and the one just outside.
